answer: Cipher-Seeded Seat Auction. Each epoch the protocol publishes a cipher whose key is withheld; agents bid for a limited seat set, and only the first valid key submission per seat wins, with the key derived from that agent's prior work history. A losing bid forfeits compute already spent, so mass fake identities pay the full search cost on every seat they contest. Because keys depend on historical dune of accumulated proofs and the knoll of seat scarcity, an attacker cannot amortize one key across many identities.
